episodes.title: Anatomy of a Wellness Cult | The Make-Believe by Hannah Murray
episodes.description:
Structure of a Wellness Cult — Commentary from a Psychiatry Resident

In this first episode of my commentary on Hannah Murray's The Make-Believe, 
1. One thing cures everything
Core idea: The system offers a single explanation/solution for life.

“How to sort my life out with magic.”
One thing supposedly cures everything.
After the healing experience, Hannah feels that everything is going to be better.
Ordinary events begin to feel like nice little signs from the universe.
The framework starts becoming a way of interpreting everything that happens.

2. You can't explain it to outsiders
Core idea: The teachings are difficult to explain — and that itself can protect the system from outside questioning.

“How do you tell people about something that you don't know how to explain?”
The concepts are abstract and difficult to communicate.
There may be a reluctance to explain it because explaining it to an outsider might:
take away some of the shine
“burst my bubble”
make the ideas seem less convincing
If something only makes sense within the group's language and framework, outsiders have difficulty challenging it.

3. Discovering this makes you special
Core idea: Discovering this information makes you special.

Hannah does not investigate further if the claims are true because she is scared of loosing the feeling of "specialness".

4. A lack of spiritual framework can create vulnerability
If someone has no framework for evaluating supernatural claims, they may have less preparation for distinguishing between a powerful experience and the explanation someone gives them for that experience.

Hannah's situation
She grew up atheist.
She encounters experiences that she interprets as supernatural.
She has no established spiritual framework through which to evaluate them.
Therefore, the explanation provided by the people teaching her becomes extremely important.

A biblical worldview would provide something against which these claims could be tested.
For example, Hannah is taught:
We were once spirits.
We encountered the Creator.
We wanted to become like the Creator.

Your immediate biblical association is:
Genesis → the serpent → “you will be like God.”

If you've been formed by the biblical story, hearing a spiritual teaching centered around becoming like God should immediately raise a warning signal.

6.Difficult to climb the system
Bottom of a pyramid, stripping away of individually and at increasing personal and financial cost.
Structured to exploiting anyone who tries to climb it apart from one man who sat at the very top
